tagline: An old turnpike through Connecticut's iron corner.
intro: US 44 crosses from Millerton, New York, and runs to Lakeville on the line of the old Salisbury and Canaan Turnpike. Route 41 joins it for under two miles through Salisbury center, and then it goes on alone toward North Canaan, about nine miles in all.

This corner of the state made iron from before the Revolution until about 1920. Its mines were small and far from any river that could carry the iron cheaply, so the town worked it into wrought iron fine enough for gun barrels and cast it into railroad car wheels. The mines are under water now.

moments.title: Lakeville
moments.text: The village was called Furnace Village until 1846, for blast furnaces that included one Ethan Allen set up in the 1760s, and it holds Lake Wononscopomuc, the deepest natural lake in Connecticut.

moments.title: Salisbury Center
moments.text: Main Street runs from the green and the White Hart Tavern of about 1800 down to the 1894 stone Scoville Library, the first library in the country open to the public free of charge.
